ⲉⲧϣⲁⲭⲍ̄ qualitative possibly from ϣⲱⲕϩ̄ 'be deep'; with ⲡϩⲛⲟⲩⲛ 'the Deep' (in glossary) it functions as the bottomless/unfathomable Deep — the archetypal cosmic depth being likened to the river's depth.

ⲡⲓ-†ⲟⲩ = 'this five' (collective demonstrative + numeral). Translated 'all this five-fold whole cosmos.' Manichaean cosmology recognizes a five-worlds structure (cf. ⲡⲉϩⲧⲟⲩ ⲛ̄ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ 'the five worlds' in accumulated vocabulary); here applied to flesh-worlds.

ⲡⲥⲟⲍⲉ uncertain — appears to function as a dimension-noun paired with ⲭⲓⲥⲉ 'height' in the four-fold dimensional series. Tentatively translated 'stature,' possibly related to ⲥⲱϩⲉ 'stand/erection' giving 'standing-up, stature.' Could alternatively be 'extent' or 'summit.' The four-fold sequence is height/breadth/length/depth — ⲥⲟⲍⲉ functions as the height-correspondent of the mountain.

ⲡⲓⲧⲁⲩ functions plurally here (collective demonstrative referring to 'these mountains'); ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲉ 'of one' = 'of one of them.' Translated 'one of these mountains.' Confirmed by line 23 ⲡⲟⲩⲉ ⲡⲟⲩⲉ ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲩ ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ 'each one of all of them.'

ⲡϣⲓⲏⲛⲥ tentatively translated 'length' as the third dimension in the four-fold series after height/breadth, before ϣⲓⲭⲍϥ̄ 'depth.' From ϣⲓⲏ 'length, dimension' + possessive marker. The four dimensions together (height/breadth/length/depth) constitute the standard cosmic-spatial inventory.
ⲡϣⲓⲭⲍϥ̄ = 'depth/abyss' (cf. ⲡϣⲓⲭϩ 'abyss/pit' in accumulated vocabulary). The fourth and final dimension. Same lexeme appears in possessed forms ⲧⲉϩϣⲓⲭⲍϩ (var. spelling) and ⲡⲉϩϣⲓⲭⲍϩ.
ⲱⲙⲕ̄ 'swallow up, be sunken' (cf. accumulated ⲁⲱⲙⲥ̄ 'submerge'). Conjunctive 3pl future-of-purpose: 'that they may be swallowed up' — describing humans relative to the cosmic sea.

ⲡⲕⲁⲣⲁⲓ̈ⲧ 'the silent (one)' (cf. ⲡⲕⲁⲣⲁⲓ̈ⲧϩ 'the Stillness' in accumulated vocabulary, here without final ϩ); ⲛ̄ⲥⲉⲍⲟⲩ conjunctive 3pl + ⲥⲁⲍⲟⲩ (Lyc ⲥⲁϩⲟⲩ) 'curse.' The damaged context prevents identifying the curser/cursed; preserved literally.

Tentatively rendered 'utter blasphemy concerning her' — ⲍⲁⲣⲡⲧⲥ̄ analyzed as Lyc. variant of ϩⲁⲣⲱⲥ̄/ϩⲁⲣⲁⲧⲥ̄ 'concerning her, before her' (preposition + 3sg.f suffix). The antecedent 'her' is likely Sophia (cf. line 12 explicit blasphemy ⲁⲧⲉϩⲥⲟⲫⲓⲁ).

Rendered 'common-sort' tentatively. The lexeme is unidentified; possible analyses include Greek βάναυσος 'common, mechanical, vulgar' (cf. accumulated tentative ⲕⲉⲃⲁⲩⲟⲛⲉ from earlier pages) or a Lyc. native term for ordinariness/multiplicity. Flagged as uncertain.

Tentatively parsed as ⲡⲉⲧⲛⲁ-ⲇⲣⲟ-ⲧⲟ̄ⲁⲧ 'he who shall prevail (over) the measure/equality': ⲇⲣⲟ 'prevail' (in glossary) + ⲧⲟ̄ⲁⲧ 'equality, proportion' (in glossary). The full phrase 'master the proportion in nothing of what is fitting' suggests a critique of those who unjustly claim mastery.

ϥⲙⲁϩ = present 3sg.m of ⲙⲟⲩϩ 'fill' or qualitative-relative '(that which) fills'. Idiom 'fill the cause/occasion of every sin' = '(he/it) is the comprehensive ground of all sin' — the position of those who blaspheme by attributing sin to God.

Rendered 'of calamities/evils' tentatively. The form ⲟ̄ⲁ̈ⲓⲉ may be Lyc. for ⲱⲁⲓⲉ 'misdeed, calamity' or related to ⲟⲩⲁⲉⲓⲉ 'fault, debt'. Negative semantic-field secured by paralleling ⲭⲱⲍⲙⲉ ⲛⲁⲣⲭⲱⲛ 'defilements of the archons' and ⲇⲁⲓⲙⲱⲛ 'demons'.

ⲛ̄ⲓⲍ rendered as 'of evil' tentatively; the lexeme is unidentified. Possible alternatives: (1) numeral 17 (ⲓ=10, ⲍ=7) yielding 'seventeen demons'; (2) Lyc. variant of ⲓⲏⲥⲉ/ϩⲟϫ 'evil, calamity'; (3) corruption. Numeral reading less likely given the listing structure (paired class-categories).
Reading as ⲥⲉ-ⲣ̄-ⲙⲛⲧⲣⲉ 'they bear witness' with scribal ⲃ̄ for ⲣ̄ (similar shape) and ⲁⲉ for ⲣⲉ. Confirmed by following ⲛ̄ⲛⲟⲩⲭ 'of falsehood' yielding standard idiom 'bear false witness against'.
Standard Kephalaia narrative-frame opener: 'Then when he had spoken/uttered this' — ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲣⲉϩ- = Lyc. ⲛ̄ⲧⲉⲣⲉϥ- temporal-perfect prefix; ⲧⲉⲟⲩⲟ 'utter, declare' (in glossary).

ⲉⲉϩ ⲛⲭⲱⲣⲉ = ⲱϩⲉ ⲛ̄ϫⲱⲱⲣⲉ 'standing strong' (qualitative + adverbial). ⲍⲓⲃⲁⲗ = ϩⲓⲃⲟⲗ 'outside' (cf. accumulated ⲍⲓⲃⲁⲗ in glossary). The fragment ⲃⲉⲛⲉ (end of unknown word) cannot be reconstructed without context.

ⲇⲉϩⲟⲩⲱ tentatively analyzed as Lyc. ⲣⲉϥ-/ⲣⲉϩ-ⲟⲩⲱⲍ '(one who) adds, proceeds' or ⲁϩ-ⲟⲩⲱⲍ 'he proceeded' (with Lyc. ⲇ for ⲣ). With ⲉϩⲉⲓⲁⲉ = ⲉ-ⲍ-ⲉⲓⲁⲉ 'to bring forth/lead' yields 'and moreover he proceeded to bring forth.'

Reading 'matter outside' as a topic-naming phrase opening the chapter, perhaps continuing from previous page. ⲍⲓⲃⲁⲗ = ϩⲓⲃⲟⲗ 'outside.' The construction may name the cosmic 'matter outside' the realm of the Greatness.

Translated 'having come inward' as circumstantial of 'come' + ⲉⲣⲟⲩⲛ 'into.' The cosmic-revelatory descent of the Light into the world. Alternative: 'come (and pass) inward' as part of ⲟⲩⲱⲛⲍ̄ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ doublet.
= ⲁ-ⲡⲁⲅⲁⲑⲟⲛ 'to/for the Good' (Greek ἀγαθόν), with regular Lyc. ⲫ for ⲑ. The apostles are sent on behalf of the Good through successive generations.
Lyc. ϩⲱⲱⲥ '(it)self, also' — 3sg.f reflexive/intensive pronoun referring to ⲡⲕⲉⲕⲉ 'the Darkness.' 'The manner also/itself in which it exists.'

ⲣ̄ⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲁϣⲓⲡⲉ = 'put to shame' (per accumulated vocabulary). With directional ⲁ- 'unto/upon': the Light shames the power (ⲧⲃⲁⲙ = ⲧ-ϭⲟⲙ) of the Darkness. Continued in line 11 with ⲁϥⲃⲣⲟ ⲁⲣⲁϩ 'he prevailed over it.'

ⲁⲧⲧⲁϣ = 'to the boundary'; ⲛⲧⲟⲩ = 'of-them' (3pl genitive) referring back to the molded humanity (Adam, Eve, and their generations). The fourth point teaches that the apostles came to the boundary of their (the molded ones') death.

Tentatively parsed as ϣⲁⲛⲧⲉ- 'until' + ϩⲃⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲛ (uncertain — possibly Lyc. for 'they reach/approach there' from ϩⲱⲛ 'approach') + ⲛϥⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'and he brings.' The soul's escape from the flesh-bound death-state. The lexeme ϩⲃⲛⲍⲏⲛ awaits parallel attestation.

'The gate of Amente (the underworld) which is at the upper side.' Standard Manichaean cosmography: there is an upper gate of Amente through which redeemed souls ascend, distinguished from the gate that descends into the abyss.
ⲥⲱⲍⲡ = ⲥⲱⲡ⳿/ⲥⲱϩⲡ 'shut up, seal' (Lyc. ⲍ for ϩ). 'They were sealed inside it' — the gate through which the redeemed pass closes behind them, sealing the soul into the upper realm.

Translated 'fetters' tentatively per vocabulary discussion. The dark powers 'bind fetters with a great bond' upon the Good and Righteousness, concealing them from view. Could alternatively be 'garments/coverings' or a class of dark beings. Confidence low.

Lyc. ⲁⲭⲙ̄/ⲁⲭⲛ = ⲉϫⲙ̄/ⲉϫⲛ̄ 'upon' (with ⲭ for ϫ; cf. ⲁⲭⲙ̄ ⲡⲥⲧⲁⲩⲣⲟⲥ 'upon the cross' line 25). Translated 'upon': the dark powers cover (= conceal by spreading their fetters) upon the Good and upon Righteousness.

Reading ⲣ̄-ⲍⲏⲃⲉ = ⲣ̄-ϩⲏⲃⲉ 'mourn, lament' (Crum 657a). 'The Cross of Light, who laments in the All' — the suffering Light/Jesus patibilis hidden in matter, lamenting cosmically. Fits the Manichaean theology of Christ's cosmic suffering. Alternative reading 'who is hidden' (ⲣ̄-ϩⲏⲡ) is excluded by the visible ⲃ at line 26 start.
